hints.text: Start from the swap rule between the two units: $\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$.
The angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ is one third of $\pi$, so take one third of $180^\circ$ by dividing by $3$.

explanation: The swap rule between radians and degrees is $\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$.
The angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ is $\pi$ cut into $3$ equal pieces, so cut $180^\circ$ into $3$ equal pieces too.
Dividing gives $180 \div 3 = 60$, so the angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ radians equals $60^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Swap pi for 180
steps: Since $\pi$ radians is the same turn as $180^\circ$, replace the $\pi$ in the angle with $180^\circ$.
The angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ becomes $\frac{180^\circ}{3}$, which is a plain division.
Dividing gives $180 \div 3 = 60$, so the angle is $60^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a quick table
steps: List the common slices of a half turn: $\pi = 180^\circ$, $\frac{\pi}{2} = 90^\circ$, $\frac{\pi}{3} = 60^\circ$, $\frac{\pi}{4} = 45^\circ$, $\frac{\pi}{6} = 30^\circ$.
A larger number under $\pi$ means the half turn is cut into more pieces, so each piece is smaller.
The row for $\frac{\pi}{3}$ reads $60^\circ$, and three such pieces rebuild the half turn: $3 \times 60 = 180$.
